title: Lightly Fried Middle-Eastern Rice Upside-Down Maqluba
description: A yeasty, snappy, crowd-pleaser middle-eastern dish featuring seasoned rice vinegar.
instructions: In a medium bowl, whisk together yeast, eggs, and 1/2 cup of warm water. Let it sit for 5 minutes until frothy.
In a large saucepan, heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil over medium heat.
Add 2 cups of uncooked rice to the saucepan and stir to coat the rice with oil.
Cook the rice for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it's lightly toasted.
In a separate bowl, whisk together lemon juice, apple cider vinegar, dried rosemary, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper.
Add the yeast mixture to the saucepan with the rice and stir to combine.
Pour the vinegar mixture over the rice and yeast mixture, and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover the saucepan with a tight-fitting lid.
Simmer the rice for 15-20 minutes, or until it's cooked and the liquid has been absorbed.
Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Using a spatula, loosen the cooked rice from the saucepan and transfer it to the skillet.
Press the rice mixture into the skillet to form a flat layer.
Fry the rice for 5-7 minutes on each side, or until it's lightly browned and crispy.
Serve the Maqluba hot, garnished with chopped fresh herbs if desired.
